title: How major US stock indexes fared Monday 10/26/2026

How major US stock indexes fared Monday 10/26/2026
The Associated Press
Mon, October 26, 2026 at 4:13 PM EDT 1 min read
^GSPC
^DJI
^RUT

U.S. stocks climbed amid a shaky day for markets worldwide, as AI stocks keep swinging and Brazilian stocks tumble.

The S&P 500 rose 0.7% Monday. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 0.3%, and the Nasdaq composite climbed 0.8%. AI-related stocks remained unsettled following weeks of sharp swings.

Later this week will come earnings reports from nearly one out of every three stocks within the S&P 500. The Federal Reserve and other big central banks will also announce their latest decisions on interest rates. Brazilian stocks tumbled following a surprise reelection for Brazil's president.

On Monday:

The S&P 500 rose 53.09 points, or 0.7%, to 7,676.77.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 146.42 points, or 0.3%, to 52,361.58.

The Nasdaq composite rose 214.04 points, or 0.8%, to 26,169.38.

The Russell 2000 rose 10.53 points, or 0.4%, to 2,786.42.

For the year:

The S&P 500 is up 831.27 points, or 12.1%.

The Dow is up 4,298.29 points, or 8.9%.

The Nasdaq is up 2,927.39 points, or 12.6%.

The Russell 2000 is up 304.52 points, or 12.3%.

title: Update: Anthropic's IPO Filing Boosts Tech Risk Sentiment, Lifts US Equity Indexes
detail:
PREMIUM
Update: Anthropic's IPO Filing Boosts Tech Risk Sentiment, Lifts US Equity Indexes
MT Newswires
Mon, October 26, 2026 at 3:55 PM EDT 1 min read
ANTH.PVT
^GSPC
^DJI
^IXIC

(Updates with index/price moves from the first paragraph.)

US equity indexes advanced as Anthropic's initial public offering filing lifted risk sentiment for big tech, especially chipmaker-related businesses.

The Nasdaq Composite jumped 1% to 26,207.2, the S&P 500 advanced 0.8% to 7,681.5, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 0.2% to 52,334.7 ahead of Monday's close.

All but three sectors rose, led by technology, consumer discretionary and financials. Communication services, healthcare, and consumer staples declined.

Anthropic filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on Monday for an initial public offering of Class A common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol "ANT." Anthropic could have a market capitalization of about $1.5 trillion, down from about $2 trillion that investors expected after the company disclosed some financial details earlier this month, Reuters reported. Goldman Sachs (GS) and Morgan Stanley (MS) are the lead underwriters, according to the filing.

Fifteen of the 20 top-performing stocks in a category with a market capitalization exceeding $200 billion each were technology firms, according to Finviz-compiled data. A majority of the top outperformers were semiconductor-related firms, including chipmaker Arm (ARM), which was up 6.7%.

The second-biggest gainer in this category was Tesla (TSLA), with shares surging 5.8% after the company said in a social media post on X that Latvia has authorized the electric vehicle manufacturer's full self-driving (supervised) system in the Eastern European nation. Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley were among the outperformers, up 2.3% and 2.7%, respectively.

The front-month West Texas Intermediate crude oil contract slid 0.8% to $102.43 per barrel, and global benchmark Brent edged down 0.2% to $116.49 per barrel.

title: Anthropic's Upcoming IPO is Buoying Markets After Steep Losses. Stocks Rebounded.
detail:
Anthropic's Upcoming IPO is Buoying Markets After Steep Losses. Stocks Rebounded.
Demian Bio
Mon, October 26, 2026 at 4:01 PM EDT 2 min read
ANTH.PVT
^DJI
^GSPC
^IXIC

Stocks climbed on Monday as investors bought the dip following a string of losses, buoyed by Anthropic's latest step toward making its IPO.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 0.29%, while the S&P 500 did so 0.70%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite overperformed, climbing 0.82%.

Anthropic is asking investors to finance its artificial intelligence ambitions while warning that its technology could cause a catastrophe so costly that insurance might be unable to cover the damage.

The developer of Claude disclosed the risk in paperwork made public Monday for its planned initial public offering. The prospectus outlines potential real-world harm from advanced AI, including systems attempting to avoid shutdown, and acknowledges that contractual protections may not shield the company from legal liability.

Anthropic devoted 94 pages of its registration statement to risk factors. Among them was a warning that the scale of damage from a catastrophic AI incident could leave the company unable to secure sufficient insurance. The filing also suggested potential losses could exceed the capacity of an individual insurer and possibly the insurance industry collectively.

The disclosures place safety concerns at the center of Anthropic's anticipated stock market debut. The company plans to list on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, although the initial prospectus does not specify an offering price.

Elsewhere, Microsoft has become the latest large company to reduce its workforce over the artificial intelligence boom, offering buyouts to tens of thousands of employees.

The company said that some 60,000 employees are eligible for the buyout. Those reached are in the U.S., Canada, India and the UK and have an experience level of 70 or below.

Amy Coleman, Microsoft's executive vice president and chief people officer, said in a memo that the program "reflects an important part of how we're evolving our approach to change: creating greater flexibility and, where possible, more ways for employees to shape their next chapter."

"This builds on what we learned earlier this year through the Voluntary Retirement Program," she added. Those who will accept the offer must make the decision over the next weeks and will leave at the end of the year.

In the geopolitical realm, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu pushed President Donald Trump to launch strikes against Iran before the countries' elections, but he has chosen to delay any action for now, according to another report.

"Netanyahu really wanted and tried to convince Trump for a joint attack in Iran before the elections, and Trump did not give a green light," an Israeli source told CNN.

Trump has not made reference to the alleged requests, but did say on Sunday that he is near deciding whether to make a deal with Tehran or "finish it off." "Do I finish it off, which would be very easy to do, or do I make a deal? It's getting to be decision time," he told Fox News.
